rationale: RE-EVALUATED IN THE CORROBORATION CORRECTION PASS. The prior draw suppressed this card under the M5 10 trigger 'all accessible pivot tiers SINGLE-SOURCE-INDICATIVE', reasoning that the broker slice 'is a different price basis' and so not a corroborating second source for the cash-index pivots. That reasoning is withdrawn. M5 5.2a and M5 10 (module_sha f69b2cd) now state that the flag describes the provenance of the H/L/C actually used to compute the tier, not the provenance of any figure quoted elsewhere in the report, and that a tier computed from the execution price series - the broker series the resulting order is filled and settled against - is CORROBORATED by construction, because that series is the settlement source rather than a secondary quote about the market and there is nothing for a second source to corroborate it against. The gate exists for tiers struck from narrative or aggregator quotes whose true prior-period H/L cannot be established. The prior draw's own arithmetic - that the slice differs from the report's quoted 28 July range by 0.88 on the high and 1.96 on the low - is beside the point: those are the report's quoted figures, and the tier below is not built from them. PIVOT TIER RECOMPUTED AND ITS CORROBORATION FLAG: the daily floor-pivot tier is recomputed from the broker execution price series in data/slices/US500/US500_upto_2026-07-28.csv (last bar 2026-07-28 23:45:00 broker), prior period = the D-1 US500 cash session of 2026-07-28 (16:30-23:00 broker), H 7452.90 / L 7384.60 / C 7433.60. Corroboration flag: CORROBORATED. Series named: the US500 broker price series carried in that slice, the series this card's order would be filled and settled against. Session named: the 2026-07-28 cash session. Levels: P = (H+L+C)/3 = 7423.70; R1 = 2P-L = 7462.80; R2 = P+(H-L) = 7492.00; R3 = H+2(P-L) = 7531.10; S1 = 2P-H = 7394.50; S2 = P-(H-L) = 7355.40; S3 = L-2(H-P) = 7326.20; and the M5 4a midpoints R1.5 = (R1+R2)/2 = 7477.40 and S1.5 = (S1+S2)/2 = 7374.95, which inherit the parent tier's CORROBORATED flag. Identity self-check R2-P = P-S2 = H-L = 68.30 and R1-P = P-S1 = 39.10, both hold. The report's own Section 11 pivots are built on the 27 July session, which is D-2 and stale for a 29 July report; they sit roughly 24 points low (its P 7399.39, R1 7438.79) and are not used. Prior-week pivots on the same corroborated basis, from the fully completed week 20-24 July 2026: P 7437.53, R1 7499.77, R2 7587.73, R3 7649.97, S1 7349.57, S2 7287.33, S3 7199.37 - also CORROBORATED, same series, sessions 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-24. So it is not the case that every accessible pivot tier is indicative, and the M5 10 corroboration trigger does not fire. SUPPRESSION TESTS RE-RUN. (i) Pivot corroboration (M5 10 / 5.2a): daily and weekly tiers are both CORROBORATED as above. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. (ii) Conviction NEUTRAL (M5 10): that trigger names Trade 1 only, and M5 5.2 states Trade 2 is fully regime-driven and does not inherit the Section 2 score, so it does not reach this card. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. (iii) RANGE without dual gate: the regime label is TRANSITION, not RANGE, so no SurfaceContractError arises. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. (iv) Qualifying swing (M5 4b): that trigger governs Trade 3A and 3B, not this card. Outcome: NOT APPLICABLE. (v) R band: on the recomputed tier the M5 5.2b geometry gives R = 27.27 points = 0.38x ATR(14) cash and 0.33x on the full broker-day ATR of 81.61, inside the 0.3x-3.0x band on both bases, so the geometry is not self-defeating and this is not a ground either. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. (vi) TRANSITION breakout-side restriction (M5 5.2 / 5.2c, with M5 3 and 3b): FIRES. This is the ground on which the card is suppressed. M5 5.2 states that if the regime is TRANSITION 'the only permitted Trade 2 is a breakout-side entry beyond the boundary; a limit on the counter side is suppressed, not re-labelled', and M5 5.2c states that Trade 2 is allowed only on the breakout side 'as identified by Trade 3C'. Trade 3C on this date is itself ineligible under M5 4d - the 28 July reference close 7433.60 is 167.37 points below the upside confirmation level 7600.97 and 148.67 above the downside level 7284.93, so no boundary has been broken and 3C emits a suppressed row. With 3C ineligible there is no identified breakout side for this card to align with. Trigger tested: TRANSITION Trade 2 with no breakout side identified by Trade 3C. Value tested: 3C eligibility = FALSE (reference close 7433.60 against boundaries 7582.80 / 7303.10 and confirmation levels 7600.97 / 7284.93). Outcome: FIRED. WHY THE PIVOT GEOMETRY CANNOT STAND IN. The M5 5.2c configuration mirrors the 5.2b breakout row on R1/R1.5/R2, which on the corroborated tier gives entry P + 0.10 x (R1-P) = 7423.70 + 3.91 = 7427.61, structural stop P - 0.8 x (P-S1) = 7423.70 - 23.36 = 7400.34, R = 27.27 points, targets R1 7462.80 / R1.5 7477.40 / R2 7492.00 and invalidation on a daily close back through P 7423.70. Every element of that ladder is well formed - stop below entry, ladder ascending, R inside the band, TP1 35.19 points from entry against the 181.65 cap, and the entry 5.99 points below the reference close so a buy limit is correctly sided. It is still not issuable, because it is not a breakout entry: 7427.61 sits 155.19 points inside the 7582.80 upper boundary, in the middle of the very range the transitional read says has not yet broken. Issuing it would be borrowing TREND geometry into a TRANSITION branch, which M5 5.2 names a construction defect even where the resulting levels are internally consistent, and it would front-run the 3C breakout the regime is waiting on. The card is therefore not forced into existence; it is recorded as a suppressed row with the trace above carried in words only and no price in any level field. rationale: RE-EVALUATED IN THE CORROBORATION CORRECTION PASS; THE SUPPRESSION STANDS ON A DIFFERENT AND VALID GROUND. The prior draw suppressed this card for want of a confirmed break - correctly - but also carried forward the report's Section 19 single-source-indicative flag onto the 25-session boundaries on the reasoning that they are prior-period highs and lows. That flag statement is withdrawn here. Under M5 5.2a and M5 10 (module_sha f69b2cd) the flag describes the provenance of the values actually used, and both boundaries below are recomputed from the broker execution price series - the series any resulting order is filled and settled against - so they are CORROBORATED by construction and there is nothing for a second source to corroborate them against. The correction does not change the outcome for this card, because the ground that suppresses it is a price test, not a provenance test. The slice settles it at 2026-07-15. CONFIRMATION THRESHOLD RECOMPUTED: M5 4d requires a settled daily close beyond the boundary by at least 0.25 x ATR(14). 0.25 x 72.66 = 18.17 on the cash basis, so the upside arming level is 7582.80 + 18.17 = 7600.97 and the mirror downside level is 7303.10 - 18.17 = 7284.93. On the full broker-day ATR of 81.61 the quarter-ATR buffer is 20.40 and the upside level would be 7603.20; the outcome is the same on either basis. SUPPRESSION TESTS RE-RUN. (i) Confirmed break (M5 4d / M5 10, 'No confirmed break per 4d in TRANSITION regime'): FIRES. This is the ground on which the card is suppressed, and it is a price test on the corroborated series, wholly independent of the corroboration gate. Trigger tested: no confirmed break beyond a 25-session boundary. Value tested: reference close 7433.60 against the upside arming level 7600.97 (short by 167.37 points) and the downside level 7284.93 (above it by 148.67); the close sits at 46.7 percent of the range width. Checked across the whole block as well: the highest cash close in the 25 sessions is 7575.20 and the lowest 7354.90, so no session in the block closes beyond either boundary, let alone beyond it by a quarter of the ATR. Outcome: FIRED. (ii) Corroboration (M5 10 / 5.2a): the boundaries are CORROBORATED as above, and in any case that trigger names Trade 2, not this card. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. (iii) Conviction NEUTRAL: that trigger names Trade 1 only. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. (iv) Qualifying swing (M5 4b): M5 4b and M5 10 both state expressly that 3C remains available when no qualifying swing exists, its anchor being the 25-session boundary rather than the swing; in fact the swing does qualify at 2.07x ATR. Outcome: NOT APPLICABLE. (v) RANGE without dual gate: the label is TRANSITION. Outcome: DOES NOT FIRE. The card is not forced into existence: M5 5.3 requires that where the selected variant's own eligibility test fails the outcome is the SUPPRESSED row for that variant, never a substitution and never pivot levels standing in for range levels. ARMING CONDITION, COMMENTARY ONLY: a settled daily close at or above 7600.97 would arm the long side; a settled daily close at or below 7284.93 would arm the mirror short. Neither is an order and neither is carried in the level fields. The report reaches the same finding in words - it prints 'Not yet met - trade pending trigger' - and then publishes a full ladder anyway, with the arming price 7598.55 standing in the entry field. That remains the defect this regeneration corrects: an arming price is not an entry. CONSTRUCTION TRACE ONLY (no prices carried into the level fields): on the corrected width the structural stop would sit inside the range at low + 0.40 x width = 7303.10 + 111.88 = 7414.98, the first target at the broken boundary plus 1.0 x width and the second at plus 1.5 x width, with invalidation on a daily close back inside the range past the midpoint 7442.95. Noted as a live conflict for any future arming: a first target one full width beyond the boundary would sit 279.70 points, or 3.85x ATR(14), from an entry at the boundary - outside the 2.5x ATR(14) target cap of 181.65 - so such a card could not be emitted on the measured move as written and would have to be scaled to the cap with the deviation stated. That is the same breach that produced the original card's far-target warning.
